title: Pork and Rice with Tomato-Based Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Pork and rice with tomato-based sauce (1307) is a dish composed of tender pork pieces, boiled rice, and a flavorful sauce made from tomatoes and spices. The meal provides protein, carbohydrates, and B‑vitamins, while the tomato sauce adds antioxidants and a tangy taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomato sauce is often prepared from fresh tomatoes, tomato paste, and a touch of sugar to balance acidity.
Pork is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide and appears in many culinary traditions.
Traditionally the dish is served hot, garnished with fresh herbs such as parsley or cilantro.
The rice‑and‑meat combination offers lasting satiety thanks to slowly digestible carbs and protein.
In some regions vegetables like bell pepper, onion, or carrot are added to the sauce for extra flavor.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Pork provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Energy‑providing carbohydrates
items.content: Rice supplies complex carbs that release energy gradually.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish contains thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Lycopene and antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, which helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Pork and the sauce provide iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Pork can contain saturated fats; choosing lean cuts and moderate portions is advisable.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Tomato sauce often includes added salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or their derivatives.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Pork must be cooked thoroughly to eliminate the risk of salmonella and trichinella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, mixing pork pieces with fluffy rice and drizzling the tomato sauce over. Garnish with fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon, or a dash of hot sauce if desired. It works well as a main course for lunch or dinner.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C. The dish can be frozen for up to 2 months, preferably portioned beforehand.
